title: Started building my first ever 3D game at 59 years old (only my second game ever!)
author: loontoon
selftext:
I just turned 59, I've not really played many games in the past 43 years as I've not owned a console or a gaming PC since I was in my mid teens.  

I've been into computers for 48 years, but have never had any formal coding education, built quite a few wordpress sites including ecommerce and managed some quite big projects in Laravel and Wordpress.  Ran a web design agency in Hong Kong, now I live in Bangkok.

Can't find any work so I decided to build a game. 

I'm using Godot with Claude and OpenCode doing the scripting, while I handle the concept, the ideas for different game mechanics etc 

I'm about 12 days in (probably 6 days of work), I have a complete 3D level designer, 12 test level to check the various game mechanics.

It's lots of fun 😄

comments.author: Due-Huckleberry-2222
comments.body:
I love it 
Best of luck be sure and share it with us.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body: Thank you!  I will be sharing stuff soon 😄

comments.author: popodwich
comments.body: It's so exciting to make game development accessible to gamers. Enjoy the journey, and best of luck with your project!

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
Thank you so much!   

I can't wait to see what other people will create with AI in the future.

comments.author: Netherfireforever
comments.body: That's awesome, love seeing devs of all ages jump into game dev. The combo of your web dev experience and AI tools is actually a really solid foundation - you already understand systems and logic, you just need to learn the game-specific patterns. One tip: don't be afraid to let Claude help you refactor as you go, because code that works for a prototype often needs restructuring when you start adding more mechanics.

comments.author: IndieRex
comments.body: How are you using Claude with Godot? Any particular MCP?

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
I just checked and Claude said - For this project I'm not actively using any MCP servers — all the Tower Maze work has been done with the built-in tools (Bash, Read, Edit, Write, etc.) running against your local repo and the Godot binary.

* **Claude Code Remote** — scheduling/triggers and session management (CronCreate, create\_trigger, send\_later, list\_environments, etc.)

I thought I had installed an MCP for Godot but apparently its not in this project. 

I'm about to fix that!

comments.author: Melodic_Theory9439
comments.body: respect — starting 3D as your second game is the part i'd gently flag, since 3D adds a whole axis of problems (cameras, lighting, navmesh, asset pipeline) on top of game logic, and that's where most first 3D projects stall out. the thing that saves people your stage is brutal scope-cutting: one mechanic, one small level, finish it ugly, then polish. nobody who quit did so because the art was bad, they quit because the scope was a marathon they planned as a sprint. what's the core loop you're building the game around?

replies.author: wizardstar1
replies.body: I agree with scope cutting. But tbh the 3d stuff for ai is no big deal as long as using good prompting and a good engine dependant on game. I started building with AI and it can be good and bad all depends on prompts and good testing. The rest is token limits that slows me down.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body: Token limits have only been an issue a few times, I use OpenCode when I hit my Claude Pro limit but its rarely happens.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
I've been in tech most of my life and have a very analytical mind.  I've written 200 page technical spec documents so developers have a complete guide to the project before a line of code was written.  

Now the developers are Claude and Qwen via OpenCode.

I've spec'd out 9 or 10 different mechanics for my game from working electrical system to power in game lights, lifts, gates etc. A working water/hydraulics system for opening gates and other things, a Train system to carry large objects between levels, when the player cannot, a crane mechanism and I'm now designing a diesel refueling mechanism for the train, the electrical generators and the crane.  Multiple floor types, launchers, portals, full 3d lighting of course.  Everything works great.

The game can be played in isometric 3D or in full immersive 3D. 

And much more.  

You play a sentient ball trapped in an environment full of machines and objects, each level is a puzzle where the player needs to figure out how to get to the next level.  The end goal will be to repair a damaged space ship and escape back to your family on your home planet.

I've been working on it for about 2 weeks, although not full time. 

I've also built an indepth level editor with more features than the actual game.  

I demoed the game at a game dev co-working space here in Bangkok last Sunday and everyone was amazed at how much I'd done already.   

The only thing missing at the moment is polish, but I'm focusing on the game itself first.  I'm aiming for a Steam preview by October and full release in November.

I'm very familiar with scope creep, but I think I've got all the mechanics and game logic set for this version.

replies.author: wizardstar1
replies.body: How do you find codex compared to claude? I am only worried about claudes token hunger tbh.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
I'm not using Codex. I'm on Linux and Codex doesn't work, or at least I've not managed to get it working.  I cancelled my OpenAi accounts anyway. 

I use Claude Pro and OpenCode, both in my Linux terminal.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body: Thanks!

replies.author: loontoon

Wow that looks amazing!  

How long have you spent on it to get to that stage?

comments.author: Epyx911
comments.body: I'm 54...lot of us Gen X  it seems :)

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
Excellent.  I've not really played games since I was in my mid to late teens.    
  
My computer timeline started at 11 years old with access to a Research Machines 380Z at school for which some of us wrote a text version of space invaders, then my parents bought me an Atari 400, followed by a Sinclair Spectrum Plus, then I got an Amiga A1000, followed by multiple A2000s and A3000s that I used to run a Fidonet BBS in Hong Kong, my final Amiga was an A4000T just after Commodore folded.    
I briefly had an Xbox (the black one with lime green logo) but hated console games because there was no piracy and games were too expensive. 

Once I started working and going out to bar and clubs for my fun, I stopped playing games.  I found girls far more interesting ;-)  

Now I'm retired and AI allows me to do things that I otherwise wouldn't be able to I figure I'd try bringing a game idea to life.

comments.author: SubjectNo2985
comments.body: Good luck, since today, i have my first demo on steam.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body: What's the link, I'd love to check it out.  How long did it take you to get it to a stage where you felt it was ready to put on Steam?

replies.author: SubjectNo2985
replies.body:
Sure! Here it is: 

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4859700/By\_My\_Side/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4859700/By_My_Side/)

Took me about 4 intense weeks total, solo, using Godot. Honestly started out wanting to make another small Android app, ended up building a full survival game instead 😄 Demo just went live yesterday, still very early days but happy to share where it's at. Would love any feedback if you give it a spin!

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
That's amazing for only 4 weeks of work.  I love the idea and your characters and graphics look great.

Makes my game look very average 😢   My game started as a simple html game for mobile devices, where you'd use the tilt of your device to roll a ball around.  I made a few demo levels in html before I realised html and js was holding me back - [https://tower-maze.purpleprawn.com/](https://tower-maze.purpleprawn.com/)You can use a mouse to control it if on a computer.

Then I switched to Godot and the game idea expanded.  But it's still a ball just with a lot more mechanics in the game.

replies.author: SubjectNo2985
replies.body: That's a cool little game, controls feel really smooth. Burned to ash on my first run though 😅 gonna give it another shot later.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback.  

I'll be posting some links to the Godot build which might feel different when playing.

comments.author: Interesting-Yellow-4
comments.body: Most fun I'm having making games is building the tools (map editor, menu editor, item editors etc). I just put a texture generator in my map editor. This is the real "game" for me right now. If the product ends up fun as well - even better :)

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body: I totally get this!  I think my game will be fun, but I'm having more fun creating the level designer at the moment.

comments.author: Imaginary_Store6090
comments.body: age is no barrier to passion

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body: Very true!  I have a good friend here in Bangkok who is 32 years younger than me and we're both working on games.
